packet.headline_seed: First plane carrying passengers evacuated from hantavirus-hit cruise ship has left Tenerife – Europe live
packet.description_seed: Spain has begun the evacuation of the first passengers from the MV Hondius ship which arrived in Tenerife on Sunday Passengers begin evacuating cruise ship hit by hantavirus In other news, there are reports of Russian attacks continuing on Ukraine despite a ceasefire that was meant to run from Saturday 9 May to Monday 11 May. There are reports of people being injured by Russian strikes in areas including the Kharkiv, Dnipropetrovsk and Kherson regions. Continue reading...

what: First plane carrying passengers evacuated from hantavirus-hit cruise ship has left Tenerife – Europe live

clean_source_blocks.text: The cruise ship linked to a deadly Hantavirus outbreak arrived early Sunday off the Spanish island of Tenerife, where the evacuation of passengers is expected to begin. Passengers will be tested by Spanish health authorities to ensure they are asymptomatic before being transported ashore in small boats, Spanish officials said, according to Reuters. Evacuation is expected to begin between 7:30 a.m. and 8:30 a.m. local time, with Spanish nationals disembarking first, followed by passengers of other nationalities, Reuters reported. They are then expected to be taken to the island’s main airport and flown back to their home countries. Multiple Americans are believed to be aboard the MV Hondius. Fox News Digital previously reported that the U.S. government is planning to transfer American passengers to a military base in Nebraska for quarantine and monitoring.

Passengers stand next to a Spanish government plane after disembarking from the hantavirus-stricken cruise ship MV Hondius at the airport in Tenerife, Canary Islands, Spain, Sunday, May 10, 2026. (AP Photo/Arturo Rodriguez)Arturo Rodriguez/The Associated Press The first plane carrying passengers evacuated from the hantavirus-hit cruise ship departed from Tenerife in Spain’s Canary Islands on Sunday, headed for a military hospital in Madrid. Spanish nationals were the first to leave the ship, which was anchored off Tenerife. They will be under quarantine when they reach Madrid, Spanish health authorities say. Only Spanish nationals will quarantine in the country. The cruise operator Oceanwide Expeditions listed 13 Spanish passengers and one Spanish crew member on board.

Nobody among the more than 140 people on the MV Hondius is showing symptoms of the virus, Spain’s health ministry, the World Health Organization and cruise company Oceanwide Expeditions said. Passengers and some crew members of other nationalities will be evacuated throughout Sunday into Monday. Six Canadians now isolating at home after exposure to hantavirus Those disembarking and personnel working at the port...

This is an excerpt from an article by Fox News Digital’s Michael Sinkewicz. Passengers were seen disembarking the hantavirus-stricken cruise ship wearing personal protective equipment (PPE) on Sunday. Video captured passengers dressed in medical masks, gowns and medical hair nets as they left the cruise ship and boarded smaller boats off the coast of the Spanish island of Tenerife. Spanish nationals were the first to disembark from the ship, though officials said passengers and some crew members of other nationalities will be evacuated throughout Sunday into Monday. The Associated Press contributed to this report. Spanish nationals were the first to leave the hantavirus-hit cruise ship, which was anchored off Tenerife in Spain's Canary Islands.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: Fox News]
The cruise ship linked to a deadly Hantavirus outbreak arrived early Sunday off the Spanish island of Tenerife, where the evacuation of passengers is expected to begin.

Passengers will be tested by Spanish health authorities to ensure they are asymptomatic before being transported ashore in small boats, Spanish officials said, according to Reuters.

Evacuation is expected to begin between 7:30 a.m. and 8:30 a.m. local time, with Spanish nationals disembarking first, followed by passengers of other nationalities, Reuters reported.

They are then expected to be taken to the island’s main airport and flown back to their home countries. Multiple Americans are believed to be aboard the MV Hondius.

Fox News Digital previously reported that the U.S. government is planning to transfer American passengers to a military base in Nebraska for quarantine and monitoring.

This is an excerpt from an article by Fox News Digital’s Michael Sinkewicz.

Passengers were seen disembarking the hantavirus-stricken cruise ship wearing personal protective equipment (PPE) on Sunday.

Video captured passengers dressed in medical masks, gowns and medical hair nets as they left the cruise ship and boarded smaller boats off the coast of the Spanish island of Tenerife.

Spanish nationals were the first to disembark from the ship, though officials said passengers and some crew members of other nationalities will be evacuated throughout Sunday into Monday.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

Spanish nationals were the first to leave the hantavirus-hit cruise ship, which was anchored off Tenerife in Spain's Canary Islands.

Spanish health authorities confirmed that the first plane carrying the Spanish passengers has departed for a military hospital in Madrid, where they will be under quarantine. Only Spanish nationals will quarantine in the country.

The cruise operator Oceanwide Expeditions listed 13 Spanish passengers and one Spanish crew member on board.

All passengers aboard the ship are asymptomatic, officials said, noting that “this unprecedented operation is going as planned.”

Passengers from France, Canada, Netherlands, the U.K., Turkey, Ireland and the U.S. were to begin disembarking next, according to the officials.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

---

[Lähde: CBC.ca]
Spanish Health Minister Mónica García said a plane carrying Spanish passengers has left and is heading to Madrid, where they will be evaluated at a hospital.

Passengers of the MV Hondius from France, Canada, Netherlands, United Kingdom, Turkey, Ireland and the United States will soon be able to leave the ship, Garcia said.

Canadian consular officials have so far declined to tell CBC News how the Canadians will be getting home.

We still haven't heard from Canadian officials on whether Canada is chartering a plane for its four passengers still on the ship.

WHO epidemiologist Maria Van Kerhove said at a news conference Saturday that Canada and the U.S. were considering sharing a plane, but neither country has confirmed whether that will happen.

Dr. William Schaffner, an infectious disease specialist at Vanderbilt University in Nashville, said if that were to happen, it would be "an example of countries collaborating for efficiency."

"We are undoubtedly going to use a plane that has infection-control precautions built into it so that the attendants are protected in the event one of those passengers happens to be sick," Schaffner told CBC News.

As boats started to ferry the Spanish passengers back to shore, the media were moved further back while officials wearing protective suits tightened their hoods and put their masks up.

In a parking lot across from the media, we can see what appears to be the first group of passengers along with doctors. Everyone is wearing protective equipment. Tents are set up and there are two red buses, which we expect will transport the passengers to the airport.

A first group of passengers, all Spanish ‌nationals, has begun to disembark ​into a small boat ​from the cruise ship, ⁠Spain's Health Ministry said.

They will be ‌transported directly from the port in military buses to ​the airport. A Spanish government plane ⁠will then fly them to ⁠Madrid, ​where they will be quarantined, officials have said.

What COVID-19 taught us about containing the hantavirus outbreak

As a hantavirus-hit cruise ship prepares to anchor off Tenerife in Spain's Canary Islands, Dr. Lynora Saxinger, an infectious disease specialist at the University of Alberta, details how this outbreak differs from the COVID-19 pandemic and how lessons from the latter can be applied here.

While the hantavirus outbreak is unlikely to ripple out into another pandemic, COVID-19 did teach governments and health officials how to better contain outbreaks like this,

payload.title: Hantavirukselle altistuneen risteilyaluksen matkustajien evakuointi alkoi Teneriffalla
payload.summary: Ensimmäinen MV Hondius -alukselta evakuoituja matkustajia kuljettanut kone on lähtenyt Teneriffalta kohti Madridia. Espanjalaiset matkustajat poistettiin alukselta ensin, ja muiden kansallisuuksien evakuoinnin on määrä jatkua sunnuntain ja maanantain aikana.
payload.content:
Ensimmäinen MV Hondius -risteilyalukselta evakuoituja matkustajia kuljettanut kone on lähtenyt Teneriffalta kohti Madridia sunnuntaina 10. toukokuuta. Alus oli ankkuroituna Espanjan Kanariansaarilla sen jälkeen, kun se oli yhdistetty kuolemaan johtaneeseen hantavirukseen liittyvään tilanteeseen. Espanjan viranomaisten mukaan matkustajien oireettomuus tarkistetaan ennen kuin heidät kuljetetaan maihin ja edelleen jatkoyhteyksiin.

## Espanjalaiset poistuivat alukselta ensin

Evakuointi aloitettiin espanjalaisista matkustajista. Heidät kuljetettiin alukselta pienemmillä veneillä Teneriffalle ja sieltä lentokentälle. Ensimmäisen koneen määränpääksi kerrottiin sotilassairaala Madridissa, jossa Espanjan kansalaiset asetetaan karanteeniin terveysviranomaisten ohjeiden mukaisesti.

Risteilyoperaattori Oceanwide Expeditionsin mukaan MV Hondiuksella oli 13 espanjalaista matkustajaa ja yksi espanjalainen miehistön jäsen. Espanjan terveysviranomaiset ovat kertoneet, että vain Espanjan kansalaiset jäävät karanteeniin Espanjassa. Muiden maiden kansalaisten ja osan miehistöstä on määrä poistua alukselta vaiheittain sunnuntain ja maanantain aikana.

## Matkustajat testataan ennen maihin kuljetusta

Espanjan viranomaisten mukaan alukselta poistuvia matkustajia testataan, jotta voidaan varmistaa, ettei heillä ole oireita. Tämän jälkeen heidät kuljetetaan maihin pienillä veneillä. Paikalta julkaistujen tietojen mukaan matkustajat poistuivat alukselta suojavarusteissa, kuten maskeissa, suojatakeissa ja hiussuojissa.

Aluksella on kerrottu olevan yli 140 ihmistä. Espanjan terveysministeriön, Maailman terveysjärjestön ja Oceanwide Expeditionsin mukaan kenelläkään MV Hondiuksella olleista ei ole havaittu viruksen oireita. Varotoimia jatketaan silti evakuoinnin aikana, ja myös satamassa työskentelevää henkilöstöä koskevat suojatoimet on otettu huomioon.

## Muiden matkustajien paluu järjestetään erikseen

Evakuoitavien on määrä siirtyä Teneriffan päälentokentälle ja jatkaa sieltä kotimaihinsa. Aluksella uskotaan olevan myös useita yhdysvaltalaisia matkustajia. Yhdysvaltojen on kerrottu valmistelleen heidän siirtämistään Nebraskassa sijaitsevaan sotilastukikohtaan karanteenia ja seurantaa varten.

Evakuointi jatkuu viranomaisten mukaan vaiheittain, kunnes matkustajat ja osa miehistöstä on saatu pois alukselta. Keskeisiä toimia ovat oireettomuuden varmistaminen ennen kuljetuksia, kansallisuuksittain järjestetyt jatkoyhteydet sekä karanteeni- ja seurantajärjestelyt niille, joille ne on määrätty.
summary_bullets: Ensimmäinen evakuoituja kuljettanut kone lähti Teneriffalta Madridiin sunnuntaina.
Espanjalaiset matkustajat poistuivat alukselta ensin ja heidät asetetaan karanteeniin Madridissa.
Viranomaisten, WHO:n ja varustamon mukaan yli 140 aluksella olleella ihmisellä ei ole havaittu oireita.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu paketin yhteneviin tietoihin evakuoinnin alkamisesta, ensimmäisen koneen lähdöstä, karanteenijärjestelyistä ja oireettomuudesta. Venäjä–Ukraina-maininta jätettiin pois, koska se oli liveblogin erillinen aihe eikä kuulu tämän jutun ydintapahtumaan.

Paikalta julkaistujen tietojen mukaan matkustajat poistuivat alukselta suojavarusteissa, kuten maskeissa, suojatakeissa ja hiussuojissa.

Aluksella on kerrottu olevan yli 140 ihmistä. Espanjan terveysministeriön, Maailman terveysjärjestön ja Oceanwide Expeditionsin mukaan kenelläkään MV Hondiuksella olleista ei ole havaittu viruksen oireita. Varotoimia jatketaan silti evakuoinnin aikana, ja myös satamassa työskentelevää henkilöstöä koskevat suojatoimet on otettu huomioon.

## Muiden matkustajien paluu järjestetään erikseen

Evakuoitavien on määrä siirtyä Teneriffan päälentokentälle ja jatkaa sieltä kotimaihinsa. Aluksella uskotaan olevan myös useita yhdysvaltalaisia matkustajia. Yhdysvaltojen on kerrottu valmistelleen heidän siirtämistään Nebraskassa sijaitsevaan sotilastukikohtaan karanteenia ja seurantaa varten.

Evakuointi jatkuu viranomaisten mukaan vaiheittain, kunnes matkustajat ja osa miehistöstä on saatu pois alukselta. Keskeisiä toimia ovat oireettomuuden varmistaminen ennen kuljetuksia, kansallisuuksittain järjestetyt jatkoyhteydet sekä karanteeni- ja seurantajärjestelyt niille, joille ne on määrätty.

article.source_text:
The cruise ship linked to a deadly Hantavirus outbreak arrived early Sunday off the Spanish island of Tenerife, where the evacuation of passengers is expected to begin. Passengers will be tested by Spanish health authorities to ensure they are asymptomatic before being transported ashore in small boats, Spanish officials said, according to Reuters. Evacuation is expected to begin between 7:30 a.m. and 8:30 a.m. local time, with Spanish nationals disembarking first, followed by passengers of other nationalities, Reuters reported. They are then expected to be taken to the island’s main airport and flown back to their home countries. Multiple Americans are believed to be aboard the MV Hondius. Fox News Digital previously reported that the U.S. government is planning to transfer American passengers to a military base in Nebraska for quarantine and monitoring.

Passengers stand next to a Spanish government plane after disembarking from the hantavirus-stricken cruise ship MV Hondius at the airport in Tenerife, Canary Islands, Spain, Sunday, May 10, 2026. (AP Photo/Arturo Rodriguez)Arturo Rodriguez/The Associated Press The first plane carrying passengers evacuated from the hantavirus-hit cruise ship departed from Tenerife in Spain’s Canary Islands on Sunday, headed for a military hospital in Madrid. Spanish nationals were the first to leave the ship, which was anchored off Tenerife. They will be under quarantine when they reach Madrid, Spanish health authorities say. Only Spanish nationals will quarantine in the country. The cruise operator Oceanwide Expeditions listed 13 Spanish passengers and one Spanish crew member on board.

Nobody among the more than 140 people on the MV Hondius is showing symptoms of the virus, Spain’s health ministry, the World Health Organization and cruise company Oceanwide Expeditions said. Passengers and some crew members of other nationalities will be evacuated throughout Sunday into Monday.
